raw_response.summary: The lender’s protections rely on assumptions that PetIQ will generate enough EBITDA from the VIP acquisition to keep leverage within limits, maintain liquidity to service debt, avoid extra borrowing, deliver timely reports, avoid material adverse events, close the acquisition successfully, and meet EBITDA thresholds for contingent notes.

assumptions.title: Sufficient EBITDA to maintain leverage ratio
assumptions.claim: The combined business will generate enough EBITDA to keep the First Lien Net Leverage Ratio at or below the covenant maximum (4.0x through 2018, stepping down thereafter).

evidence.quote: Pro-forma for the transaction, net leverage is expected to be approximately 1.6x to 1.8x for LTM Adjusted EBITDA for the calendar year ending December 31, 2018.
The Term Loan Credit Agreement includes a maintenance covenant that requires compliance a maximum first lien net leverage ratio.

assumptions.title: Adequate liquidity to service debt
assumptions.claim: PetIQ will have sufficient cash and operating cash flow to meet interest and principal payments on the $75 million term loan and any contingent promissory notes.

evidence.quote: PetIQ plans to finance the cash portion of this transaction with $25 million of existing cash on hand and $75 million of new debt with secured financing commitments from East West Bank and Ares Capital Management LLC.
PetIQ expects incremental annual interest expense of $5.3 million associated with the financing of the transaction.

assumptions.title: No additional indebtedness beyond permitted baskets
assumptions.claim: PetIQ will not incur indebtedness outside the contractually permitted baskets, relying on its ability to restrict new debt.

relationships.rationale: If the VIP acquisition closes and performs as expected, the added EBITDA will keep the leverage ratio below the covenant maximum.
Meeting the EBITDA thresholds for contingent notes ensures any extra debt does not push the leverage ratio above the covenant limit.
Sufficient liquidity and cash flow enable debt service, preventing missed payments that would increase leverage.
Restricting additional indebtedness stops leverage from rising beyond the covenant threshold due to new borrowing.
Absence of a material adverse effect and strong retail prospects support the expectation that the acquisition will close and perform as planned.
